headline: Tk 619cr investment to reopen 3 closed jute mills, 11,600 jobs expected
summary: The government has signed lease agreements with PRAN-RFL and HAMCO Group to restart operations at three state-owned jute mills.
details: The government has signed lease agreements with two private business groups to reopen three long-closed state-owned jute mills. The move involves an investment of approximately Tk 619 crore and is expected to create at least 11,629 jobs.

Under the agreements, PRAN-RFL Group will take over the National Jute Mills Ltd in Sirajganj and Star Jute Mills Ltd in Khulna. HAMCO Group will take over the Platinum Jubilee Jute Mills Ltd in Khulna.
The three mills are expected to generate a combined potential annual turnover of about Tk 1,175 crore once they become operational again.

Specific investments are planned as follows: Tk 157 crore for National Jute Mills in Raipur, Sirajganj; Tk 250 crore for Star Jute Mills in Digholia, Khulna; and Tk 212 crore for Platinum Jubilee Jute Mills in Khalishpur, Khulna.
The government intends to reopen 20 of the 25 closed mills under the Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation (BJMC) through a lease-based private management system.
So far, leases for 14 mills have been completed and possession has been handed over to lessees, with production already resuming at nine of them.
The agreements were signed in the presence of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Secretariat, with representatives from BJMC, PRAN-RFL Group, and HAMCO Group.

headline_marked: 8.32%: [[Inflation falls to eight-month low]] in July
headline: 8.32%: Inflation falls to eight-month low in July
summary: Driven by a sharp decline in food prices, overall inflation dropped from 9.16% in June to 8.32% in July, the lowest rate since November last year.
details: According to official data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS), overall inflation fell to 8.32 percent in July, down from 9.16 percent in June.
The decline was primarily driven by a sharp drop in food inflation, which fell to 7.16 percent from 8.60 percent in the previous month, providing some immediate relief to households.
Non-food inflation also eased slightly, moving from 9.61 percent to 9.28 percent. Rural inflation stood at 8.36 percent, while urban inflation was 8.24 percent.
Despite the drop, economists warn that the easing may reflect normal fluctuations or seasonal factors rather than a sustained cooling of price pressures.
Fahmida Khatun of the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) noted that the full impact of recent electricity tariff increases may not yet be reflected in the July figures.
Mustafa K Mujeri of the Institute for Inclusive Finance and Development (InM) cautioned that non-food inflation remains high and a clear downward trend has not yet been established.
caption:
Inflation in Bangladesh has hit its lowest level in eight months. Is this a sustained cooling of prices or just a temporary dip?

According to official data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS), overall inflation fell to 8.32 percent in July, down from 9.16 percent in June.

The decline was primarily driven by a sharp drop in food inflation, which fell to 7.16 percent from 8.60 percent in the previous month, providing some immediate relief to households.

Non-food inflation also eased slightly, moving from 9.61 percent to 9.28 percent. Rural inflation stood at 8.36 percent, while urban inflation was 8.24 percent.

Despite the drop, economists warn that the easing may reflect normal fluctuations or seasonal factors rather than a sustained cooling of price pressures.

Fahmida Khatun of the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) noted that the full impact of recent electricity tariff increases may not yet be reflected in the July figures.

Mustafa K Mujeri of the Institute for Inclusive Finance and Development (InM) cautioned that non-food inflation remains high and a clear downward trend has not yet been established.
